# top_trader_fills — per-wallet coverage, snapshot 2026-10-04

Source: read-only query on the static backup
`/Users/noder/hyperliquid_backup/runs/2026-10-04T145227Z_monthly/hyperliquid.db`
(GROUP BY wallet; no live-DB queries — the bot writes that file).

Context: the pre-cursor collector fetched `userFills` (latest ~2000)
per wallet per hourly pass and was SIGINT'd at the next `:07` cron
tick — passes never finished (measured 22.9–72.0s per 2000-row
request on the congested host; ~3h for a 263-wallet pass).
This table documents the resulting coverage BEFORE the incremental
(userFillsByTime + per-wallet cursor) rewrite. Historical data left
as-is per T2.

## Aggregates

- wallets: **263** — total rows: **12,312,798**

### Staleness of `MAX(time_ms)` (days before snapshot)

| staleness | wallets | % |
|---|---|---|
| <1d | 50 | 19.0% |
| 1–3d | 35 | 13.3% |
| 3–7d | 29 | 11.0% |
| 7–30d | 44 | 16.7% |
| >30d | 105 | 39.9% |

### Row-count distribution

| rows | wallets |
|---|---|
| 0–100 | 13 |
| 100–2,000 | 39 |
| 2,000–2,100 | 102 |
| 2,100–50,000 | 77 |
| 50,000+ | 32 |

### Pass-position bias check (alphabetical = old pass order)

| third | fresh max_t (<1d) | stale (>7d) | median rows |
|---|---|---|---|
| first third | 20 | 52 | 2000 |
| last third | 18 | 45 | 2000 |

**Read:** undercoverage is NOT positional — last-third wallets are no
staler than first-third (the alphabetical universe order randomised
which wallets died mid-pass each hour). Coverage is activity-bound:
wallets with <5K rows have median staleness 40.6d (mostly dormant —
the API simply has no new fills), while the 32 wallets >50K rows are
all <1d fresh. The ~102 wallets at exactly ~2000 rows are the
`userFills` plateau — capped windows, no evidence they had more.
